name: Hannover Airport
before:
Hanover's airport, 11 km north of the city in Langenhagen, and ninth largest in Germany. It flies to European city and leisure destinations and is a base for Eurowings, Corendon Airlines Europe and TUI fly Deutschland.

The train is the easy way in. Hannover Flughafen station sits beneath Terminal C, with S-Bahn line S5 running to the city centre every thirty minutes for twenty two hours a day, taking about seventeen minutes. During the Hanover Fair an additional hourly S8 runs straight to the fairground, which is worth knowing for a trade client.

There are three main terminals, A, B and C. They are connected on the landside but each has its own separate airside area, so a passenger needs the right terminal from the start. A separate Terminal D to the east, once used by the Royal Air Force for British troop flights, has been back in use at peak times since July 2023.

Terminals A and B date from 1973 and are admired for their compact design. Sheremetyevo in Moscow was modelled on them.
after:
Hanover's airport, 11 km north of the city in Langenhagen and eighth busiest in Germany. It flies to city and leisure destinations, and Eurowings, Corendon and TUIfly are among its airlines.

The train is the easy way in. Hannover Flughafen station sits directly beneath Terminal C, and S-Bahn line S5 reaches the main station in under 20 minutes.

There are three main terminals, A, B and C, connected on the landside. The airport says departures from A and B share the security checkpoint in Terminal A, with B a few minutes' walk beyond it, while Terminal C has its own. A passenger needs the right terminal from the start.
